summary: Redwood AE+SE walked the Nova Commerce team through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown features focused on understanding token-level cost drivers, route tagging, and rollout controls. Customer asked about hosted vs dedicated economics, SSO/KMS, and how to attribute costs to product teams. Agreed next steps: share security docs, pricing, set up pilot and benchmark run.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. With me is Liam, our solution engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Ethan Brooks: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to see the console.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Great. We're planning a 45 minute walkthrough - show the usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown flows, and leave time for Q and A. Does that work?
[00:20] Sofia Ruiz: Works for us. We want to see how we can attribute costs to product teams and get alerting when a route spikes.
[00:27] Liam Patel: Perfect. Quick qualification: are you mostly on hosted right now or considering dedicated/private?
[00:32] Sofia Ruiz: We're on a mix - PoCs are hosted, but for production we expect to move to dedicated or private in some cases because of data residency.
[00:40] Priya Singh: Also curious about KMS/HSM integration and SSO. Need audit logs.
[00:45] Liam Patel: Totally. We'll point those out. Okay jumping into the console - first screen is the Usage Overview. You can see total tokens, request counts, and cost over time.
[00:56] [01:05] Liam Patel (screen): Here is a time series; we surface model-level and route-level cost. In the middle you can filter by route tag or project, e.g., checkout-flow, search-api, recommendations.
[01:20] Sofia Ruiz: Can we group by product team? We have multiple teams using the same endpoints.
[01:24] Liam Patel: Yes - via route tags and labels. You can attach tags to requests at the SDK or proxy level and the console aggregates per-tag. The per-route dashboard shows token split, avg latency, P95, and cost-per-1000 tokens.
[01:39] Ethan Brooks: How accurate is the cost attribution? We use VMs for other workloads and need near-real cost accounting.
[01:45] Liam Patel: We calculate cost using per-token unit rates we host, plus any dedicated capacity allocation if you're on Redwood Dedicated. It's best-effort: we attribute by route and model variant; for dedicated we also allow allocation of GPU pool costs to teams using linear or weighted assignment.
[02:00] Priya Singh: That's helpful - do you have examples of cost spikes and root cause?
[02:05] Liam Patel: Yeah, here's a recent customer example - a re-routed model causing extra long context windows. You can use the per-request sampling to see example prompts, and filter on sequence length to isolate high-cost calls.
[02:20] [02:28] Sofia Ruiz: The sampling - is that PII safe? We can't surface whole user prompts.
[02:33] Liam Patel: Good call. Sampling can be redacted and we support token-level hashing or only include metadata fields. For enterprise we can redact or only store aggregated statistics.
[02:45] Ethan Brooks: About routing: can we send high priority traffic to lower-latency hosts and low priority to cheaper variants?
[02:52] Maya Chen: Yes, smart routing supports latency/cost policies and fallback to compatible model variants. You can define route policies in console and they show metrics side-by-side.
[03:05] Sofia Ruiz: We need to enforce SLOs per route - will alerts map to those?
[03:10] Liam Patel: Alerts tie to per-route SLOs; console can create alerting rules on latency, error rate, or cost thresholds and push to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhooks.
[03:20] [03:30] Priya Singh: If we go private/on-prem, do we still get the console and dashboards?
[03:35] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private includes a control plane that can be run in your VPC and the console connects over private networking. For fully air-gapped we provide an on-prem bundle and offline reporting options.
[03:48] Ethan Brooks: On security - SOC2, ISO, do you have certs and audit logs?
[03:52] Liam Patel: We have SOC2 Type II; we'll send the attestation. Audit logs are available per request with retention policies; KMS integration for key management and HSM for private customers on request.
[04:05] Sofia Ruiz: Good. Show us a live per-route cost breakdown please.
[04:10] [04:15] Liam Patel (screen): Here - selecting route 'search-api'. Top-left is cost per day, then tokens broken out by prompt vs completion, next is average cost per call. You can toggle model variant, quantization level, and batching settings to see simulated cost changes.
[04:30] Sofia Ruiz: Nice - can we run "what-if" scenarios? Like change batching from 8 to 32 and see cost/latency trade-offs?
[04:36] Liam Patel: Absolutely - the Optimize tab simulates batching, tokenization effects, and quantization recommendations. It also shows expected end-to-end latency impact.
[04:45] Ethan Brooks: How do you estimate latency with batching? We worry about tail latencies.
[04:50] Liam Patel: We model queuing and service time based on your traffic distribution. The console shows P50/P95/P99 estimates and you can enable continuous profiling to compare to live runtimes. For tail latencies we recommend a hybrid policy: keep a small reserved pool for low-latency requests and batch others.
[05:10] [05:16] Sofia Ruiz: For billing, can we export route-level invoices so product teams can be charged back?
[05:20] Maya Chen: Yep - we provide per-route export CSV and will integrate with your billing system; many customers use route tags to do internal chargebacks.
[05:28] Priya Singh: Any limitations with the SDK tagging? We use a serverless proxy layer that strips headers sometimes.
[05:34] Liam Patel: You can attach tags at the SDK, proxy, or server side. If headers are stripped, server-side tagging or a proxy extension works. We have examples for Lambda and Envoy.
[05:45] Ethan Brooks: Competitors often mask cost signals - how is Redwood different?
[05:48] Maya Chen: We focus on per-route transparency, unit economics controls, and built-in recommendations for batching/quantization so you can actively reduce cost while tracking SLAs.
[05:58] [06:05] Sofia Ruiz: Let's talk pilot. Timeline: we'd like a 2-week pilot with production-like traffic. Can you run benchmarks?
[06:12] Liam Patel: Yes - we can do a benchmark run against a clone of your traffic patterns. We'll need 2 weeks of traffic patterns and a list of high-volume routes. We'll also set up a small dedicated pool if you want realistic allocation.
[06:25] Maya Chen: We'll schedule an initial setup call with engineering and provide a runbook. We'll also share pricing scenarios for hosted vs dedicated.
[06:33] Priya Singh: One more - RBAC? We need fine-grained roles for billing, devs, and infra.
[06:38] Liam Patel: Console supports SSO with SAML/SCIM and fine-grained RBAC - you can restrict who can change routing or see raw prompts.
[06:46] [06:50] Ethan Brooks: Anything else on integrations? We use Datadog for APM - can we push metrics there?
[06:55] Liam Patel: Yes, metric exporters for Datadog, Prometheus, and direct traces.
[07:02] Sofia Ruiz: Sounds good. I want to confirm the redaction options again for sampled prompts.
[07:08] Liam Patel: We'll provide a doc. Default is to store aggregated stats, sampling is optional and can be hashed or redacted fully.
[07:16] [07:25] Maya Chen: Quick recap: we'll send SOC2 + security docs, pricing, and schedule the benchmark. You will provide traffic patterns and success criteria. Any blockers?
[07:33] Sofia Ruiz: No blockers. We'll review the materials and confirm pilot scope.
[07:38] Ethan Brooks: Thanks - that was helpful.
[07:41] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items we listed.
[07:45] [07:45] Call ends
